steps.prompt: Before the check: write one hook and one thesis about any topic you like.

cards.title: Thesis & introduction: quick review
cards.body: Claim (arguable) vs fact (checkable) vs opinion (taste). Argumentative thesis: claim + because + reasons. Informative thesis: topic + parts. Narrative focus: what the story meant. Hooks: question, surprising fact, quote, short story, bold statement; never an announcement. Background bridges hook and thesis. The thesis comes last.

cards.title: An informative introduction
cards.body: No side to take: the thesis names the topic and the parts you will explain (“… in three ways”). A surprising fact makes a great hook for an informative essay.

cards.title: How the check works
cards.body: First, a 10-question quiz: you need 8 right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see which skills to review, and you’ll get new questions next time. Then you’ll write the introduction to an informative essay. Quill gives it a score.

prompts: Which part of an introduction do you now find easiest? Which is still hard?
How will you choose your hook next time?
